source.question: q-160771
source.value: Find the domain of the vector-valued function $f(t)=\sqrt{2+t}\,i+\frac{1}{3+t}\,j+(1+{t}^{2})\,k.$

decisions.reason: Observed MA content supersedes the stored value

decisions.question: q-162685

authoring.question: q-162685
authoring.value:
To find the domain of $f$, we need the intersection of the domains of the individual components.

- The domain of the 1st component $\frac{1}{{t}^{2}-4}$ is $t\in (-\infty -2)\cup (-2,2)\cup (2,\infty ).$

- The domain of the 2nd component $t$ is $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

- The domain of the 3rd component $\sqrt{t-2}$ is $t\in [2,\infty ).$

The intersection is illustrated in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14033854/assets/18bd3e410f2f3e415e8164ae6e2f9e03a2f7281ce15e6e05cb570ecfdac10964.png)

Therefore, the domain of the vector-valued function $f(t)$ is $t\in (2,\infty ).$
